evidence.reason: At the pinned tip, `resolveLauncher` still returns a lexical `resolve(candidate)` path for both direct names and PATH candidates. The containment check canonicalizes only for its own test, so a workspace symlink whose target is outside the workspace passes, while the stored lexical path remains retargetable. If it is retargeted to a workspace file after the per-launch check and before spawn, the launcher can execute workspace-controlled code on the host before the sandbox boundary, defeating the documented “same binary” binding. Canonicalizing once at resolution and returning `undefined` on canonicalization failure is the smallest fail-closed repair and does not require an owner decision.
